To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sarcoma virus released by a murine virus-induced hamster tumor cell culture line was noninfectious, and that the virus released by another hamster tumor cell line contained the sarcoma virus genome and a helper virus.

(i) the sarcoma virus released by a hamster tumor induced with a murine sarcomavirus was noninfectious (S+H-), (ii) a second virus, which transformed hamster cells, was released from the same tumor cell line (S-), (iii) the S- virus was a pseudotype virus, and (iv) the S- pseudotype virus was derived from the S+H- virus.

HTG2 cells release noninfectious sarcoma virus particles (S+H virus), whereas HTG3 cells release hamster type C pseudotypes of murine sarcoma viruses (Gz- MSV [HaLV]), which can transform hamster but not murine cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the release of noninfectious and transforming viruses by murine sarcoma-virus-induced tumor cell lines.
the establishment of a cell culture line that releases a noninfective sarcoma virus and the subsequent activation of this virus in vitro by the introduction of a helper virus.
the properties of noninfectious and transforming viruses released by two hamster cell lines derived from a transplantable Gz-MSVs-induced tumor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Gz-MS-V (HaLV), a hamster type-C virus pseudotype of the murine Gz-MS virus, is a defective sarcoma virus.
Gz-MSVs are defective sarcomas viruses, which are unable to induce transformation of hamster cells but are capable of inducing transformation of mouse cells.
HTG2 virus, which was noninfectious, was a defective sarcoma virus without helper virus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HTG2 cell line is a nonproducer of murine sarcoma and leukemia viruses, whereas the HTG3 cell line is a producer of Gz- MSV (HaLV).
Gz-MSVs induce in vivo a variety of hamster tumor cell cultures which differ in the type of virus produced.
Gz-MSVs are capable of inducing tumors and releasing viruses in hamsters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HTG2 cells are a unique source of a noninfective murine sarcoma pseudovirus.
the HTG3 cell line is a model system in which the genome of a mouse sarcoma virus can be expressed in heterologous hamster cells.
Gz-MSVs can induce tumors in a variety of hosts and can produce a variety of type C viruses in these hosts.
